decision: Rejected: foreign templates recover many labelled kicks but create extensive false firing, including stationary bass and double firing on isolated kicks. High recall at this firing rate is not evidence of reliable kick classification. No production integration or threshold tuning.
method:
Fixed two-component spectral fitting: known-stem diagnostic and foreign templates.

This is a small NNLS mixture experiment inspired by NMF transcription, not a
reproduction of a published system. A kick spectrum competes with a strictly
past-only background spectrum. No existing v5 candidate gate is applied.
settings: 2048-point trailing Hann FFT, 30–2500Hz; native ~5.33ms hop. Kick template averaged from first five strong isolated source attacks after 1s, each first80ms. Foreign template averages other songs equally. Background is past-only80ms EMA. Exact two-column NNLS residual improvement;3/80ms power followers; ratio>2, rearm<1.2, floor1e-6, 60ms refractory. No sweeps.
decision_rule: Own-stem diagnostic should improve Heavy recall without extras in its kick/bass cores. Foreign-template support requires more associated hits, no original associated labels lost, no increase in unmatched overall or bass-only cores.

startup_checks.method: Cold-start controls, no startup exclusions; foreign-to-Heavy template from the fixed trial, no threshold changes. Synthetic falling-pitch kick is the existing controls waveform, not the template training sound.

validation: Six focused numerical/causality tests pass, including independent SciPy NNLS comparison and amplitude scaling. Every foreign template excludes its evaluation song. Source and label hashes verified. Runtime CPU cost is offline throughput only.
limitations: Own-song template is privileged diagnostic information, not generalisation. Every foreign template excludes the evaluation song. Only existing provisional short passages scored; all nine tracks are development material. Magnitude spectra are approximately additive; interference and mastering violate exact additivity. CPU timing is batched offline process time, not a native callback benchmark. No live changes.
interpretation: Templates are prepared offline from isolated stems; this experiment does not learn a kick from the incoming mix. Only the background updates during processing. Earlier source segments are privileged same-song knowledge in the Heavy diagnostic, including future knowledge relative to its bass intro. The foreign comparison excludes that song completely. A fixed spectral mean lacks attack/decay ordering; a single background spectrum cannot represent arbitrary bass or other sources. Adding a kick basis improving reconstruction is not sufficient evidence that a kick occurred.
